findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with instance or state access.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and exposing it to unauthorized access if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.
The EBS snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of its source volume, meaning snapshot data (including any copies or shares) is stored without encryption.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management port to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against the host.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no additional controls (e.g., WAF, TLS), exposing the web service directly to untrusted networks and cleartext traffic.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances in this subnet, combined with the internet gateway route and permissive security group this directly exposes the web host to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing the attack surface by exposing resources directly to the internet.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to sensitive network traffic logs.
